properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony raised this at the very end of 2026-08-09 and it got no thinking because the session was out of context. Nothing below is intent; the options are recorded so the roads not taken survive.

ANTHONY'S QUESTION, and he brought the strongest counter himself: should reflow2's management and governance surface (rules, enforcement, claims/seats, epochs, releases, readiness, budget, ownership) live where it does, or become a sister package? HIS OWN COUNTER-ARGUMENT: **UAF does not separate them** — Architecture Management, Project, Standards and Strategic are all viewpoints inside one framework. That counter is strong and is engaged below rather than waved at.

--- OPTION A — STAY UNIFIED (status quo, no work) ---
One package, one vocabulary, one graph. FOR: proj:reflow2's objective is already "Keep a design coherent from concept THROUGH OPERATIONS" — the whole lifecycle is the stated scope, so a split narrows an objective held since genesis. The management surface is DEFINED BY READING DESIGN STATE: dec:release-trigger computes a cut from what is delivered, req:readiness-gates-the-roadmap computes the epoch from readiness rather than declaring it, req:plans-move-honestly puts plan movement on the record. None of that is a layer on top; it is a reader of the coherence graph, so a sister package would need full read access anyway — at which point ask what was actually separated. AGAINST: this is also the option that requires nobody to think, which is not the same as being right.

--- OPTION B — SPLIT INTO A SISTER PACKAGE ---
A second crate / MCP server with its own vocabulary, sharing the graph. FOR, and this is the real evidence: dec:bl-155 measured 40 of 132 served tools never called, and roughly SEVENTEEN of those forty are the management/governance/coordination family (claim_region, claim_report, release_claim, mint_seat, apply_merge, merge_designs, recall_resolutions, plan_epoch, set_epoch_status, arrival_delta, budget_report, add_flow, part_of_flow, performed_in, add_resource, add_environment, set_project_mode). The management half is measurably the least-exercised part of reflow2. Also: the natural users differ — governance's natural consumer is an agent fleet, design coherence's is a person designing. AGAINST, and it is the same datum read the other way: BL-155's own conclusion is that these tools are UNREACHABLE FROM ANY SKILL, not unwanted — "a capability nobody can find is worth what an absent one is worth". Packaging is not the cause of the non-use, so packaging is not the cure; a split would make them less reachable, not more. SECOND COST, concrete: a sister package collides with two ACCEPTED requirements — req:thin-install ("after setup, a project never has to change again for reflow2 to move") and req:no-setup-per-project ("setting up a project is not a step"). The split is not free; it is paid for in install friction the design already refused once.

--- OPTION C — SPLIT THE VOCABULARY, NOT THE PACKAGE ---
One binary; governance/management becomes a declared, optional PROFILE a project opts into. FOR: this is what UAF actually does, and it is where Anthony's counter is sharper than it first looks. UAF unifies VIEWPOINTS in one framework; it says nothing about whether one piece of software ships them. So the UAF precedent argues for one VOCABULARY and is silent on one PACKAGE — which suggests the question is a packaging question wearing a vocabulary question's clothes, and that separating the two axes may dissolve it. AGAINST: reflow2 has no profile mechanism today, so this is the option with the most unbuilt machinery behind it.

--- OPTION D — NEITHER: THE LINE IS MECHANISM vs POLICY ---
Not a package boundary at all. Mechanism lives in reflow2; policy lives in each project's own graph and reflow2 stays ignorant of it. FOR: this is the line the storyflow fleet drew after a month of operations, with the test "could a solo hobbyist, a two-person team and a regulated enterprise each express THEIR governance with this, without reflow2 having an opinion about which is right?" Their verdict sizes the missing work as small: "reflow2 models the DESIGN well and the DECIDING poorly — it does not know who may decide, what a decision covers, which rules can even be checked, or where else a rule is written down. Those four are what a governance layer is, and each is a small declarative field plus a report — NOT A SUBSYSTEM." You do not split a package off four fields. AGAINST: the same report notes DesignRule is "the least-connected type in the schema, which is odd for the one whose whole job is to bind other things" — so governance here is an underfitted corner, and calling the remaining work small may be measuring the part already understood.

--- WHAT THE GRAPH ITSELF SAYS, checked rather than assumed ---
reflow2's own functional decomposition (dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition, "reflow2's systems are functional, not its file tree") holds EIGHT systems — Agent Surface, Coherence Loop, Documentation, Human Channel, Intake, Design Store, Time & History, Vocabulary — and NONE of them is management or governance. There is no existing seam to split on. That cuts both ways and the honest reading of both is recorded: it means a split must invent a boundary the design never drew, and it means the absence of that boundary may be exactly why the area is tangled.

RELATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED: dec:idea-package-versus-shared-server asks a different packaging question (shared server vs self-contained package) on the same axis; rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party governs how any answer must be judged — by what it does for a consumer's project, never for this repo.
properties.name: OPEN — should management/governance stay inside reflow2, or split into a sister package?
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming at Anthony's request (/brainstorm, 2026-08-09). Searching the graph first changed the shape of the question three times: proj:reflow2's objective already claims concept-through-operations, so a split narrows a stated scope; dec:bl-155's never-called list turns out to be ~17/40 management tools, which is the strongest datum on either side and reads both ways; and req:thin-install + req:no-setup-per-project give the split a concrete, already-accepted cost. The storyflow fleet's trial-case report (2026-08-09, api-boss 05af57c1) supplies option D from a month of live operation. No option is recommended and none is promoted to intent.
